changes.before: A system learns a decision tree from examples. Must it be a deep neural network?
changes.after: Deep learning is one kind of machine learning, which is part of AI.

before: Artificial intelligence, or AI, is a broad name for systems built to perform tasks such as recognizing patterns, planning, or generating language.
Machine learning is an approach within AI that learns patterns from data. Data means recorded examples or measurements.
Neural networks are one family of machine-learning models. Their connected calculation units will be introduced later.
Deep learning uses neural networks with multiple processing layers. It is not a name for every machine-learning method.
A decision tree is another machine-learning model: it follows learned branching questions. Not every learned model is a neural network.
after: Artificial intelligence, or AI, is a broad name for computer systems that do tasks such as recognizing pictures, planning, or writing text.
Machine learning is part of AI. It finds patterns in data: recorded examples or measurements.
A neural network is one kind of machine-learning model. It passes numbers through connected calculations.
Deep learning uses neural networks with several processing layers. A layer is a group of calculations whose results feed the next part of the network.

before: Return to the preceding idea and compare what changed.
after: Machine learning is the wider group.

before.question: A system learns a decision tree from examples. Must it be a deep neural network?
choices: Yes. Learning and deep learning mean exactly the same thing.
No. A decision tree cannot learn from data.
No. Machine learning includes model families other than neural networks.
before.explanation: Machine learning is broader than deep learning; the model family matters.

after.question: A model learns a decision tree from examples. Must it be a deep neural network?
choices: Yes. Machine learning and deep learning mean the same thing.
No, because decision trees cannot learn.
No. Machine learning also includes other kinds of models.
after.explanation: A learned decision tree is machine learning. Deep learning uses layered neural networks.

changes.before: Concept-only lesson. No programming, API key, model execution, or account connection is required. Sources support general concepts, not claims about private model internals.
